title: Local durable Workflow recovery reference product
selection_status: agent-selected prototype candidate under user-authorized R01; no product approval or production selection
rationale: Reuse the existing Python recovery planner and sqlite3 available in the local standard library; exercise separate local transaction boundaries without a database service.

runtime_observation.scope: availability only; R02 must pin the exact implementation/test runtime and dependencies

bounds.wakeup: local polling hint; duplicate or absent hints cannot change dispatch truth

storage.transaction_control: sqlite3 autocommit=True; explicit SQL BEGIN IMMEDIATE / COMMIT / ROLLBACK; do not use Connection.commit() as the commit operation
storage.attachment: No ATTACH or transaction spanning both files
storage.filesystem: local Linux filesystem with SQLite locking; network filesystems and shared multi-host storage excluded
storage.configuration_gate: Read back required pragmas and reject mismatches before writing business state; schema/profile/version mismatch stops mutation.

clock.kind: host monotonic time plus host boot identity
clock.testing: Injected shared deterministic clock at exact lease boundaries plus actual process kill/restart on the same host boot
clock.backward_or_boot_change: Stop advancement without fabricating a terminal result; retain evidence for owner-directed successor work.
clock.limit: No cross-boot resume, wall-clock adjustment tolerance claim, or multi-host clock guarantee.

identity.intent: Reuse unchanged D37 identity from existing planner
identity.plan: Freeze ordered occurrences and canonical plan digest
identity.binding: Persist exact Operation binding and implementation digest selected before dispatch; mismatch blocks invocation
identity.attempt: New durable ID and increasing per-occurrence number at each execution start; acquire/renew alone creates no attempt
identity.invocation: Reuse existing D40 identity H(intent_id, plan_digest, operation_id, plan_occurrence_id) across retries and takeover

transaction_boundaries.rule: Only participants changed by one transition join that transaction. Persist intent, exact plan and binding set before dispatch is eligible. No Operation is invoked inside this transaction.

atomic_participants: successful invocation identity and recorded result
transaction_boundaries.rule: Unique invocation identity plus exact binding/payload digest. Under one write transaction return an existing matching success or apply and record one success atomically. Same identity with different payload/binding rejects. A failed pre-commit call records no applied-success row; durable attempt evidence lives in coordination. No network or external business effects.

claim_and_lease.acquire: Bootstrap claim or takeover uses version CAS. Takeover requires expired/released authority, increments durable fence and supersedes prior claim; active claim acquisition is rejected. These are store arbitration transitions, not unfenced worker progress.
claim_and_lease.advance: At transaction authorization point check expected version, current claim/fence, latest lease generation and valid_from <= now < expires_at; serialize transition through commit; no user callback or wait inside it. Recheck time immediately before committing and reject expired authority.
claim_and_lease.renew: Same current claim and fence, greater lease generation; no revival after expiry.
claim_and_lease.loss: After invocation starts, loss of effective authority produces unknown, even if a late callback reports success. New claimant records unknown during takeover before any successor attempt. Old worker commits are rejected.
claim_and_lease.safety_limit: An expired worker may already be inside an Operation; fencing protects coordination commits while the Operation-owned ledger protects repeat business application.

retry.selection: Frozen example Operation binding explicitly selects retry for failed/unknown attempt outcomes; separate fixtures select escalate and terminal-failure. Failure classification alone cannot select retry.
retry.budget: At most three durable execution starts per occurrence, counting failed, unknown and successful starts. Reserve the next number atomically when starting. Claim and lease changes consume none.
retry.schedule: Before eligibility, persist predecessor attempt, unchanged identity/binding, selected policy, next number, remaining budget and not-before = selection_time + 1000 ms.
retry.unknown: Reconcile durable stores before further invocation. A committed matching Operation result may supply evidence for progress under a new valid claim. Otherwise replay only under the frozen explicit retry policy and budget. If reconciliation cannot establish state, retain unknown and stop that run.
retry.exhaustion: With three starts consumed and no durable success evidence, record exhausted with consumed-budget evidence; do not claim no business effect happened.
retry.store_failures: Busy/conflict before transition commits is no advancement and no new attempt. A later poll rereads state. Ambiguous commit requires reread/reconciliation; no blind replay. Corrupt or inaccessible state stops that run with not_evaluable dependent checks.

terminal.completed: Durable success evidence for every occurrence; semantic state satisfied.
terminal.exhausted: Explicit terminal-failure continuation or consumed retry budget with no reconciled completion; semantic state unresolved.
terminal.escalated: Explicit Operation-owned escalation continuation; semantic state unresolved; record route, do not send messages or launch another workflow.
terminal.rule: Record terminal evidence and semantic projection atomically in coordination. Terminal rejects retries and implicit successors.

claims.liveness_conditions: Eligible work, available healthy stores, advancing clock, polling worker, valid binding, and remaining budget; no universal eventual completion.
